summary: Web Summit founder Paddy Cosgrave drew widespread outrage from Israeli and international tech figures after posting criticism of Israel's response to the Hamas attacks without initially condemning Hamas. Speakers, investors and Israel's ambassador to Portugal announced cancellations or boycotts ahead of the Lisbon event. Cosgrave issued a statement condemning Hamas but then reasserted that war crimes should be called out, and Web Summit said it expects to max out at 70,000 attendees.
one_line: Paddy Cosgrave's posts criticizing Israel's response to Hamas triggered boycotts and cancellations from tech leaders ahead of Web Summit in Lisbon.
key_facts: Web Summit's flagship Lisbon event is next month and is expected to "max out" at 70,000 attendees; last year's drew about 71,000.
Web Summit will hold its newest event in Doha, Qatar, in four months' time.
Paddy Cosgrave was in Doha on the day Hamas attacked Israel and posted data on X about the human cost of the Israel-Palestine conflict between 2008 and 2023, omitting the weekend's events.
Hamas killed 1,400 people, mostly civilians, and took 199 hostages back into Gaza in the attack.
On Friday Cosgrave said he was "shocked by the rhetoric and actions of so many Western leaders" in supporting Israel.
David Marcus, fintech entrepreneur and Meta executive, said he would never attend, sponsor or speak at a Web Summit event again.
Keith Rabois of Founders Fund said he would refuse to work with anyone who speaks at the Qatar conference for the rest of his career.
Ori Goshen, co-founder and co-CEO of AI21 Labs, said he would not give his keynote and AI21 would not attend, using #cancelwebsummit.
Israeli ambassador to Portugal Dor Shapiro wrote to the Mayor of Lisbon saying Israel will not participate and that dozens of companies had already canceled.
Cosgrave nine days after the invasion condemned the Hamas attacks and hoped for peaceful reconciliation, then tweeted: "War crimes are war crimes even when committed by allies... I will not relent."
Josh Kopelman of First Round Capital suggested Cosgrave is in the pocket of Doha and Qatar, which many believe is connected to financing Hamas.
Garry Tan, head of Y Combinator, canceled his appearance, condemning Hamas and praying for peace for Israelis and Palestinians.
A public Notion page titled "techcondemingterror" tracks the growing response from Israel's tech industry.
